newsitem.title: JAPAN: Surplus unlikely to grow drastically mid-term - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Surplus unlikely to grow drastically mid-term - MOF.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus is unlikely to grow drastically in the mid-term although there may be temporary fluctuations, a Finance Ministry official told reporters on Wednesday.

Although it was difficult to make a clear prediction due to movements in currencies, oil prices, and economic conditions at home and abroad, imports were continuing to grow and and this growth was exceeding that of exports, the official said.
He said the deficit in services trade was continuing to widen.
"I think the shrinking trend of the surplus in goods and services trade will continue," he said.
He said that the pace of the decline in the overall current account figure, which includes income from Japan's investments overseas, was slowing down.
The surplus in income balance, or income from Japan's direct investments and securities investments overseas, was on a rising trend, he added.
"We don't see a drastic increase in the current account surplus in the mid-term, though there may be temporary fluctuations," he said.
